subject: physics
title: Energy resources
key_idea: Energy resources are **renewable** if they are replenished as they are used, and **non-renewable** if they are finite. They are used for transport, electricity generation and heating. Each has different reliability and environmental effects, and their use changes over time.

blocks.text: This section covers the energy resources available on Earth and the difference between renewable and non-renewable.

items.meaning: One that is being, or can be, replenished as it is used.
One that is finite: it cannot be replaced as fast as it is used.
Fuel made from plant or animal material.
A resource whose supply is predictable, so it can generate when needed.

diagram.alt: Sort each energy resource into renewable or non-renewable.

blocks.text: What the resources are used for

items: **Transport:** petrol and diesel from oil, bio-fuels, and electricity for electric vehicles.
**Electricity generation:** fossil fuels, nuclear fuel, wind, hydroelectricity, tides, water waves, the Sun and others.
**Heating:** gas and other fuels burned directly, and electricity.
Renewable resources are replenished as they are used.
Non-renewable resources are finite: fossil fuels and nuclear fuel.
The uses are transport, electricity generation and heating.

blocks.text: Resources differ in how reliably they supply energy and in the harm they cause.

items: Wind turbines do not turn when the wind is too weak or too strong.
Solar cells depend on sunlight, and fixed cells are not always pointed at the Sun.
Solar cells need a large area to generate much electricity, and the UK has limited daylight.
Fossil fuel and nuclear power stations burn or use stored fuel, so they can generate when needed, apart from maintenance. Their fuel is finite.

rows: Carbon dioxide increases global warming (the greenhouse effect). Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides cause acid rain. Particulates can harm living organisms.
No carbon dioxide produced. Radioactive waste is produced, stays dangerous for a long time and needs safe storage. There is a risk of accidents.
Visual pollution, noise pollution and danger to birds.
Land is flooded behind the dam, causing loss of habitat.

items: Wind and solar are less reliable than fossil fuel and nuclear power stations.
Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, which increases global warming.
Nuclear power produces no carbon dioxide but does produce radioactive waste.

blocks.text: The mix of energy resources changes over time. Renewables now provide a growing fraction of electricity in many countries.

items: Fossil fuels may run out, become costly or be in short supply.
Burning fossil fuels increases global warming and acid rain, so use of non-renewables is reduced.
Governments encourage solar panels with grants, and the technology is now cheaper and more efficient.
People install solar panels to reduce energy bills or sell electricity back to the National Grid.

blocks.text: Some governments close coal-fired power stations and plan nuclear ones. Nuclear power helps meet demand with less carbon dioxide.

items: Use of renewables is increasing and use of non-renewables is decreasing in many countries.
Reasons include cost, grants, finite fossil fuels and environmental damage.
Give a named effect, such as global warming, not just 'pollution'.

checks.q: Describe the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy resources.
checks.a: A renewable resource is replenished as it is used. A non-renewable resource is finite.

checks.q: Suggest two reasons why wind power could not meet the UK demand for electricity on one day.
checks.a: Wind is unreliable, or it was not windy. Wind turbines do not turn when the wind is too strong or too weak, or there are not enough turbines.

checks.q: State one harmful waste product from burning oil and one from nuclear fuel.
checks.a: Burning oil: carbon dioxide. Nuclear fuel: radioactive substances (nuclear waste).

worked_example.question:
On one day the demand for electricity in the UK was 34 000 MW.

Suggest two reasons why wind power was not able to meet this demand.
answer_points: Wind is unreliable (it was not windy on that day)
Wind turbines do not turn when the wind is too strong or too weak
There are not enough wind turbines in the UK
worked_example.tip: Any two of these points score the 2 marks.

worked_example.question:
Both using nuclear fuel and burning oil produce harmful waste products.

State one harmful waste product from each process.
answer_points: Using nuclear fuel: radioactive substances (nuclear waste)
Burning oil: carbon dioxide (or greenhouse gases, a named pollutant, or toxic gases)

worked_example.question:
Scientists are researching the World's energy use for the future.
The future demand for fossil fuels is expected to increase.

Give two reasons why scientists are worried about this increase in demand.
answer_points: Fossil fuel may run out / is non-renewable / may be in short supply / may become very costly
A named damage to the environment, for example greenhouse gases, global warming, carbon dioxide, climate change or acid rain
worked_example.tip: One mark for the supply problem and one for a named environmental damage.
